title: Nilpotent elements are the intersection of the minimal primes
statement: Let $R$ be any commutative ring. A prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset R$ is minimal if no prime ideal of $R$ is strictly contained in $\mathfrak p$. Then $\bigcap_{\mathfrak p\text{ minimal prime of }R}\mathfrak p=\{r\in R:\exists n\geq1,\ r^n=0\}$, where the intersection of an empty family of ideals is $R$. No Noetherianity or reducedness is assumed; the zero ring is allowed. Equivalently, this intersection is $\sqrt{(0)}$, where $\sqrt I=\{x:x^m\in I\text{ for some }m\geq1\}$ is the radical notation of [lem-weil-pbc-zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq].
